title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own research text. It is a page of a Bourbaki typescript, headed 'SYSTÈMES de RACINES (20)' and 'Tribu n° 59'. It drafts exercises for Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Ch. VI §4, which the published Bourbaki chapter (1968) presents in final form. It was most likely filed with, or reused as scrap paper for, the motives notes; the neighbouring pages concern motivic fundamental groups and the cohomology of Tate motives Z(i).

First part (end of the E6 exercise, R = E6):
- Let Q be the root lattice and P the weight lattice. Since P/Q ≅ Z/3, we have 3P ⊂ Q, and E = Q/3P is an F3-vector space of dimension 6 − 1 = 5.
- Because (Q|P) ⊂ Z, the Killing-normalized form reduces to a symmetric bilinear form on E. It is non-degenerate, and the reduction map R → E is injective.
- O(E) = {±1} × SO(E). The spinor norm SO(E) → {±1} has kernel SO+(E), which is simple of order 25920 (≅ PSp4(3) ≅ PSU4(2)). So O(E)/SO+(E) is a Klein four-group.
- Its three index-2 subgroups give a unique index-2 subgroup Ω(E) of O(E) other than SO(E) and not containing −1.
- Reduction gives Aut(R) = W × {±1} → O(E). Both groups have order 103680, so this is an isomorphism. It sends W(R) onto Ω(E) and W+ onto SO+(E). Hence W(E6) is an extension of Z/2 by the simple group of order 25920.

Second part (F, R = E7):
- P/Q ≅ Z/2, so 2P ⊂ Q, and E = Q/2P has dimension 6 over F2.
- (Q|2P) ⊂ 2Z, so the form descends. It is alternating because roots have even norm, and it is non-degenerate. This gives W → Sp(E) ≅ Sp6(F2), written Sp(3,F2) in the text.
- The kernel is {±1}, since −1 ∈ W(E7) acts trivially mod 2. Comparing orders (|W(E7)| = 2903040 = 2 · 2^9 · 3^4 · 5 · 7) gives exactness of 1 → {±1} → W → Sp6(F2) → 1.
- W+ maps isomorphically onto Sp6(F2), since det(−1) = −1 in rank 7. So W(E7) ≅ {±1} × Sp6(F2).
- A second proof is suggested via W(E8) (W(E8)/{±1} ≅ O8+(F2)) and the isomorphism Sp6(F2) ≅ O7(F2).
errors: No mathematical errors. 'Sp(3,F2)' denotes the symplectic group of a 6-dimensional F2-space (Sp6(F2)), an old notation convention. '(1,-1)' should be read as the subgroup {1,-1}.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a Bourbaki 'Tribu 59' draft of standard exercises later published in Lie VI. Its only interest is archival: a Bourbaki typescript page filed among Grothendieck's 1965 motives notes. It contains no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'E = Γ/3P' is probably 'E = Q/3P' (the root lattice Q, badly struck by the typewriter).
'(1,-1)' in the exact sequence denotes the group {1,-1}.
